text: If you can see the insane paper on world models, you'll understand it really easily just by looking at how these models are trained. And if you haven't seen this AI beat LLM's hundreds of times larger than it at a task that has big implications for the future of AI and robotics. And two people who built the foundation for modern AI are betting their careers on this. And one of them even said he thinks LLM's are a dead end and this is the path forward, which is exactly what he said about neural networks 20 years ago. But first, why are LLM's bad at understanding the world? And you might think they do understand the world 'cause look at all this crazy stuff they do, but they're extremely inefficient and here's why. LLM's are trained to predict the next word. Now inside of that, they have some concept of understanding because they have to adjust different words meanings based on other words around them. But the goal of predicting the next word is not the best path to actually understanding how the world works. So they were able to do that way more efficiently in like a stupidly easy to understand way. So if I tell you a puppy running by the sea and a dog playing in the beach, you're probably gonna picture about the same things. Now AI thinks of things in terms of list of numbers, not whatever's going on in our head. So they'd give a model multiple descriptions of the same scene and then trained it so it's lists of numbers or thoughts for each of those descriptions became similar. And then the crazy part was how they tested it to see if it understood the world. They took another model that they just trained on images and that model also got an understanding of what things are from the images it saw. Then they went to see which model was more similar. The large language models or the model they trained from just descriptions of images. Remember, it never saw single image only text and their model destroyed the LLMs on this comparison. And that might not seem crazy today, but the applications, especially for robotics, are huge. This is an autonomous system that needs to understand text and vision and sensors and more. And those things can all work together if they have the same world model. And that's why two people who've started the AI boom in 2012 are betting billions that the future is not in a bigger chat box.
